wave_title: Closes two named TARGET gaps in the OBSERVED BUILD dependency census: `optional = true` manifest entries now classify as DependencyKind::Optional, and dependencies declared under [target.'cfg(...)'.dependencies]/.dev-dependencies]/.build-dependencies] now classify as DependencyKind::TargetConditional. `.atlas/contracts/DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md`.

generation_model.G_n: 37533f1a2e (fix(census): disambiguate same-name multi-version Cargo.lock entries) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: self-inspection of DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md's own recorded 'Still TARGET' list, which explicitly named 'ProcMacro/TargetConditional/Optional DependencyKind emission' as declared-in-vocabulary but never emitted -- an OBSERVATION_GAP distinct from a live incorrectness, since this workspace's own manifests have neither construct today

priority_classification: dependency closure (priority 6 of the controller's own ordering) -- extends the scope of an already-materialized capability (BUILD dependency census) toward full DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md contract closure, rather than fixing a live defect (that was Generation 3, priority 1).

design_decisions.question: Should Optional/TargetConditional override the section-derived Runtime/Dev/Build kind, or combine with it?
design_decisions.decision: Override -- DependencyKind stays a single classification per edge (matching the existing enum shape and DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md's own kind vocabulary listing 'optional/feature-gated' and implicitly target-conditional as their own classes, not modifiers). A dependency that is both e.g. dev + optional is classified Optional; which table it lived in remains reconstructable from evidence_path if ever needed.

design_decisions.question: Should TargetConditional parse and represent the actual target-selector expression (e.g. distinguish cfg(unix) from cfg(windows))?
design_decisions.decision: Not this wave -- classified uniformly as TargetConditional regardless of selector. Representing the selector requires an admitted target-context matrix (DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md's own 'Resolution context' section) this bootstrap does not yet model; named explicitly as remaining TARGET rather than silently narrowed.

design_decisions.question: Does Optional here mean the dependency is actually active in some admitted context?
design_decisions.decision: No -- it means 'declared optional in the manifest text'. Feature-selection resolution (which optional dependencies a given admitted feature set actually activates) is a separate, larger resolution-context capability, explicitly still TARGET, not claimed by this wave.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: optional = true and [target.*.dependencies] manifest entries are correctly classified, and this repository's own real dependency closure is unaffected (it has neither construct).

Closes two named DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md TARGET items (Optional/TargetConditional DependencyKind emission); ProcMacro remains out of reach (requires reading a dependency's own manifest, out of this parser's scope) and resolution-context activation semantics remain explicitly TARGET.
